climate.overview_html: The UN Climate Summit 2026 entered its second and final day on September 24; on September 23 Secretary-General Guterres escalated his rhetoric, accusing major oil companies of treating the atmosphere “like an open sewer” and noting that five major Western oil firms collected nearly half a trillion dollars in profits since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Germany became the first G7 economy at the summit to announce a national roadmap to phase out fossil fuels, targeting 2045; Guterres called for tripling renewable capacity, doubling energy efficiency, sharp methane cuts, and ending deforestation. The World Resources Institute’s summit statement flagged the core finance ask: $1.3 trillion per year in climate finance flows by 2035, with at least $300 billion per year mobilised for developing countries. The Super El Niño scientific backdrop remains unchanged from September 22: Carbon Brief’s analysis showing the Niño 3.4 daily anomaly at 3.07°C on September 19 — a near-tie with the all-time daily record — two full months earlier in the seasonal calendar than the 2015 precedent. The Foster & Rahmstorf GRL >98% confidence warming-acceleration result continues to anchor Nepal’s UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA.

items.source: Climate Change News / UN News / France 24 / WRI
items.headline: UN Climate Summit 2026 Day 2: Guterres Calls Big Oil “Open Sewer” Operators; Germany First G7 Nation to Adopt Fossil Fuel Phase-Out Roadmap (Target 2045); Climate Finance Ask: $1.3 Trillion/Year by 2035; $300 Billion/Year for Developing Countries
items.summary: On September 23, UN Secretary-General Guterres delivered his sharpest remarks of the summit, accusing major oil companies of treating the atmosphere 'like an open sewer' while collecting nearly half a trillion dollars in profits since 2022. He argued the world already has the tools to end the fossil fuel age and called for tripling renewable energy capacity, doubling energy efficiency, accelerating electrification, cutting methane emissions sharply, and ending deforestation. Germany announced a national fossil fuel phase-out roadmap targeting 2045, becoming the first G7 economy to make a summit pledge of this nature. WRI's summit statement highlighted the financial architecture needed: $1.3 trillion per year in total climate finance flows by 2035, with at least $300 billion per year mobilised for developing countries — a figure echoed across summit side events and endorsed by the incoming UNFCCC Executive Secretary. The summit concludes September 24 with outcomes feeding into the COP32 negotiations track.

items.headline: Carbon Brief Analysis: Super El Niño Daily Niño 3.4 Anomaly Hit 3.07°C on September 19 — Near-Tie with All-Time Daily Record (3.08°C, 19 Nov 2015) but Two Months Earlier in Calendar; August Monthly Anomaly 2.45°C; Further Strengthening Forecast
items.summary: Carbon Brief analysis using NOAA daily SST data finds the Niño 3.4 daily anomaly reached 3.07°C on September 19, 2026 — placing it in a statistical tie with the previous all-time daily record of 3.08°C from 19 November 2015. Critically, the 2026 record arrived approximately two months earlier in the seasonal calendar, while official forecasts continue to indicate further strengthening through October–December 2026. August 2026 had a monthly Niño 3.4 anomaly of approximately 2.45°C — higher than the peak of every prior El Niño on record except 2015–16 and the 1877–78 event. Further strengthening to a new all-time record is expected before the seasonal peak in December–February.

items.headline: Super El Niño Multi-Model Forecast: 75% Probability of Strongest Event on Record Since 1950; OND 2026 Median Peak +2.67°C; 90%+ Probability Super El Niño Persists September–January; Spring 2027 Neutral Transition 55%
items.summary: Updated NOAA CPC and IRI multi-model ensemble forecasts give a 75% probability that the current Super El Niño will surpass the 1997–98 event to become the strongest on record since 1950. Median OND 2026 forecast is +2.67°C for the Niño 3.4 index. There is a 90% or greater probability of the Super El Niño phase persisting through September 2026–January 2027. A 55% probability of returning to neutral phase by April–June 2027 is consistent with historical post-Super El Niño patterns. NOAA projects a median peak of approximately 4.1°C in December — about one degree higher than the record-breaking 2015–16 event's peak.

items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: Niño 3.4 ~+3.6°C; Positive IOD +0.9°C; Above-Normal Temperatures Forecast for Most Land Areas; 2027 Still Forecast as Warmest Calendar Year on Record
items.summary: WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–November 2026 places the Niño 3.4 index at approximately +3.6°C above average, consistent with the Super El Niño at or approaching its seasonal peak. The co-occurring positive Indian Ocean Dipole at +0.9°C amplifies drought risk over Indonesia, the Philippines, and eastern Australia while increasing rainfall risk over eastern Africa and the Horn. Above-normal temperatures are forecast for most global land areas in SON 2026. WMO confirms 2027 remains the likely warmest calendar year on record as the El Niño peak contribution propagates into NH winter 2026/27.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; First Statistically Confirmed Acceleration Since ~2015 at >98% Confidence; Fastest of Any Decade in 177-Year Record Across Five Temperature Datasets
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets (NASA GISTEMP, NOAA GlobalTemp, HadCRUT5, Berkeley Earth, ERA5) to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The result directly strengthens the attribution basis for the Nepal–Tibet UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission active at UNGA this week.

weather.overview_html: The most operationally significant development: INVEST 91W has continued to organize as of September 24, having moved to approximately 173 nautical miles west-southwest of Guam; the JTWC Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert remains active with scatterometry showing a tightening low-level circulation and convection in all quadrants under favorable environmental conditions — TD formation is expected within 24 hours. The bigger casualty update comes from Nepal: Nepal’s government raised the number of missing persons from approximately 3,916 to approximately 6,150 on September 16, with the confirmed dead standing at approximately 1,400 across Nepal and Tibet combined — a roughly 60% increase in the missing toll from what was reported in the immediate aftermath. In the Atlantic: the 2026 Atlantic season’s record for the longest hurricane-free stretch in the satellite era — surpassing September 18, 1966 — remains intact as of September 24, now extended to at least six days beyond the previous record, with Super El Niño wind-shear attribution confirmed. In Southeast Asia: the Philippine government has issued a health advisory as haze from Indonesian fires reaches Metro Manila; over 300,000 ha have now burned across Borneo and Sumatra, and CAMS senior scientist Mark Parrington warned that “if fire emissions continue to increase, as would be expected through September into October, the smoke and air quality impacts could persist for several weeks across the region”.

items.headline: INVEST 91W UPDATED September 24: TCFA Active; System ~173 nm WSW Guam (~12.5°N ~139.0°E); Tight LLC With All-Quadrant Convection; Favorable Shear, 29–30°C SSTs; TD Formation Expected Within 24 Hours; NW Track Projected; No Direct Marianas Threat
items.summary: INVEST 91W has continued to track westward and organize as of September 24, now positioned approximately 173 nautical miles west-southwest of Guam — farther west than its September 23 position of 127 nm south of Guam. The JTWC Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert remains active, with scatterometry confirming a tightening low-level circulation surrounded by convection in all quadrants. Environmental conditions remain highly favorable: vertical wind shear at or below 15 knots, good equatorward outflow aloft, and warm sea surface temperatures of 29–30°C. Global models remain in consensus on tropical depression formation within the next 24 hours with a continued northwestward track. No direct threat to the Marianas Islands is forecast. If it develops into a named storm it would become the 26th named system of the 2026 West Pacific typhoon season.

items.source: Wikipedia / ABC News / Al Jazeera / SANA
items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Floods UPDATED: Missing Toll Raised to ~6,150 on September 16 (Up From ~3,916); ~1,400+ Confirmed Dead in Nepal and Tibet Combined; Rehabilitation Phase Ongoing; UNFCCC Loss and Damage Submission at UNGA
items.summary: Nepal's government raised the official missing persons count from approximately 3,916 to approximately 6,150 on September 16, 2026 — a near-doubling of the missing toll. The confirmed death count stands at approximately 1,400 across Nepal and Tibet combined, with at least 1,451 deaths reported by Nepal alone per the Wikipedia summary and 43 deaths plus 519 missing in Tibet's Autonomous Region. The event was triggered on August 26 by a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung that produced catastrophic debris flows along a 72 km stretch of the Trishuli River; seismometers recorded Ms 5.2 tremors. The Nepal government remains in the rehabilitation and reconstruction phase. Nepal's UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission, citing the Foster & Rahmstorf GRL warming acceleration result, is active at UNGA this week.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane-Free Streak Extends Past September 24: Record for Longest Hurricane-Free Run in Satellite Era (Post-September 18, 1966) Now Extended >6 Days Beyond Previous Record; Super El Niño Wind-Shear Attribution Confirmed
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season's streak of zero hurricane formations extends through at least September 24, now more than six days beyond the previous satellite-era record of September 18, 1966. Tropical Storm Fay became post-tropical on September 23 without reaching hurricane intensity. The season's six named storms (Alex through Fay), all at tropical storm strength or below, reflect Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear across the main development region. NOAA forecasts indicate the below-normal pattern will persist through at least October as the Super El Niño continues to strengthen.

items.source: Mongabay / CAMS / Philstar / Asian News Network
items.headline: SE Asia Wildfire Haze UPDATED September 24: Philippines Government Health Advisory Issued; >300,000 ha Burned in Indonesia; 12 Million+ People Across Six Countries Blanketed; ASEAN Level 3 Alert; Smoke Could Persist Through October
items.summary: The Philippine government has issued a formal health advisory as haze from Indonesian fires reaches Metro Manila, adding a sixth nation to the affected zone alongside Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. More than 300,000 hectares have burned across Borneo and Sumatra per Nusantara Atlas data. CAMS senior scientist Mark Parrington warned that if fire emissions continue to increase as expected through September into October, smoke and air quality impacts could persist for several weeks across the region. Indonesia's Health Ministry recorded 113,336 respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of September 9. The ASEAN Level 3 (highest) haze alert remains active. Conditions are consistent with the worst Indonesian fire season in 11 years, driven by Super El Niño-suppressed late rainy season onset.

items.headline: Pakistan Monsoon Flood Death Toll UPDATED: 907 Dead / 1,044 Injured Nationwide Since Late June Per NDMA (September 6 Figure); Flash Flooding Ongoing in Sindh, KPK, GB, Punjab; Final Monsoon Active Phase
items.summary: Pakistan's NDMA as of September 6, 2026 reported 907 dead and 1,044 injured across the country since monsoon onset in late June — substantially higher than earlier-reported episode-specific figures. House collapses account for approximately 48.6% of fatalities; drowning and flash flooding are the other leading causes. The worst-affected provinces remain Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab. Urban flooding has inundated parts of Lahore, Rawalpindi, and Faisalabad. Approximately 2 million homes have been damaged or destroyed and an estimated 1 million livestock have perished. The final monsoon active phase extends through late September, with additional heavy rain systems forecast over Sindh and KPK.

renewables.overview_html: WindEnergy Hamburg 2026 moves into its penultimate day on September 24 with Hall B3 dedicated entirely to next-generation specialists; yesterday’s headline remained RWE’s call for Europe-wide CfD indexation (up to €4.4 billion in savings across Germany’s 9 GW pipeline), and the event closes September 25 with more than 1,600 exhibitors and 43,000 participants. The largest single deal of the week: Enel completed its $760 million acquisition of an 810 MW US solar portfolio from Excelsior Energy Capital on or around September 11 — the assets include the 525 MW (AC) Faraday solar plant in Utah County backed by a 20-year PacifiCorp PPA with Meta as off-taker, and the 100 MW (AC) Skyhawk plant in Tennessee backed by a TVA PPA — generating an estimated $90 million per year in EBITDA. India’s grid build-out continues: CTUIL issued the Transmission Service Agreement for a 2 GW Solapur renewable energy evacuation project on September 23. IEA projects global energy investment reaching a record $3.4 trillion in 2026, with $2.2 trillion in clean energy and grid investment approaching $550 billion.

items.source: PV Magazine USA / Renewable Watch / Mercom Capital
items.headline: Enel Closes $760 Million Acquisition of 810 MW US Solar Portfolio from Excelsior Energy Capital; 525 MW Faraday Utah (Meta Off-Taker, 20-Year PacifiCorp PPA) + 100 MW Skyhawk Tennessee (TVA PPA); ~$90 Million Annual EBITDA; Part of $1.3 Billion Wind+Solar Tranche
items.summary: Italian energy major Enel completed the acquisition of an 810 MW portfolio of US solar assets from Excelsior Energy Capital at an enterprise value of approximately $760 million, with the transaction closing on or around September 11, 2026. The portfolio consists of two solar plants: the 682 MW DC (525 MW AC) Faraday solar plant in Utah County, Utah, backed by a 20-year Schedule 34 green energy PPA with PacifiCorp (Rocky Mountain Power), with Meta acquiring a substantial share of the generation and associated environmental attributes; and the 127 MW DC (100 MW AC) Skyhawk plant in Obion County, Tennessee, backed by a long-term TVA PPA in commercial operation since 2023. The combined assets are expected to generate approximately $90 million per year in EBITDA. The deal is part of a broader agreement signed in February 2026 for over 1 GW of wind and solar with total enterprise value of approximately $1.3 billion; the remaining 205 MW of wind capacity is expected to close in Q4 2026.

items.headline: RWE at WindEnergy Hamburg September 22: Calls for Europe-Wide CfD Indexation for Offshore Wind; Up to €4.4 Billion in Savings for Germany’s 9 GW Pipeline by 2030; €2 Billion Potential Savings for 4 GW Tendered in 2027
items.summary: RWE's head of offshore wind development for Belgium and the Netherlands called at a NedZero panel at WindEnergy Hamburg on September 22 for Europe-wide adoption of indexation for offshore wind Contracts for Difference. The mechanism — already implemented in the UK and Belgium — links contract strike prices to inflation indices over the operating term. For Germany's 4 GW planned for tendering in 2027, potential cost reductions are estimated at up to €2 billion; for Germany's full 9 GW tender pipeline through 2030, the figure rises to up to €4.4 billion. WindEnergy Hamburg runs September 22–25, 2026 with more than 1,600 exhibitors and 43,000 participants from 100 countries.

items.headline: CTUIL Releases TSA for 2 GW Solapur Renewable Energy Evacuation and Transmission Expansion Project (India) — Selected Bidder Gets 10-Day Window to Execute Agreement and Acquire 100% SPV Equity
items.summary: Central Transmission Utility of India Ltd (CTUIL), a subsidiary of Power Grid Corporation of India, released a Transmission Service Agreement on September 23, 2026, for a 2 GW renewable energy evacuation and transmission expansion project in Solapur, Maharashtra. Following issuance of the Letter of Intent, the selected bidder will have 10 days to execute the TSA and pay the acquisition price for 100% equity shareholding in the Special Purpose Vehicle. The project is part of India's large-scale grid reinforcement program to evacuate power from the Solapur solar and wind zones — a critical bottleneck for India's 500 GW renewable target by 2030.

items.headline: 50Hertz Awards LanWin3 2 GW North Sea HVDC Converter Platform to NSORe + Siemens Energy — Second 2 GW NSORe/50Hertz Contract in 2026; Combined LanWin3 + LanWin6 Value ~€2.5 Billion; Topside Rostock-Warnemünde, Jacket Vlissingen
items.summary: German TSO 50Hertz awarded the LanWin3 North Sea offshore HVDC converter platform contract to the Neptun Werft–Smulders Offshore Renewables (NSORe) JV and Siemens Energy on September 18. This is NSORe's second major 50Hertz contract in 2026, following LanWin6 in June. Siemens Energy supplies the high-voltage components; NSORe handles design, procurement, construction, offshore installation, and commissioning. Combined NSORe value for LanWin3 and LanWin6 totals approximately €2.5 billion.

items.headline: LS Marine Solution Wins 156.9 Billion Won (~US$114 M) Submarine Cable Contract for 390 MW Sinan Wooi Offshore Wind Farm — South Korea’s First National Growth Fund Project; Largest-Ever LS Marine Order; First in 8.2 GW Sinan Belt
items.summary: LS Marine Solution secured a 156.9 billion Korean won (~US$114 million) contract on September 18 to supply and install submarine power cables for the 390 MW Sinan Wooi offshore wind farm — its largest-ever order at 2.2 times its full-year FY2025 revenue. Sinan Wooi is the first project to receive funding from South Korea's National Growth Fund for offshore wind, and marks the opening project in the government-designated 8.2 GW Sinan offshore wind development belt. Cable installation is scheduled 2026–2028.

science.overview_html: Two operationally significant ML weather models moved into focus this week. WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582, September 3, Google DeepMind + Google Research) is now running operationally at 0.1° resolution, generating new forecasts every hour by ingesting raw low-latency geostationary satellite data — the first global AI weather model to match physics-based NWP on both spatial and temporal resolution while directly assimilating observations, and it currently powers Google Search and Google Maps weather feeds. AICON (arXiv:2608.24651, August 25, Deutscher Wetterdienst) describes the GNN-based 13 km, 3-hour-step model that has been running operationally at DWD since March 2, 2026, trained on the high-resolution ICON-DREAM dataset using an icosahedral multi-mesh that preserves fine-scale fidelity by avoiding multi-step rollout during training. Also new today: arXiv:2609.27290 (September 23, Chegini et al.) introduces a physics-informed neural network for sparse-observation atmospheric thermal forecasting constrained by a pressure-coordinate thermodynamic advection–source equation, demonstrating mean RMSE improvement over baselines growing from 8.1% at one hour to 23.8% at three hours in an Oklahoma development case — a direct proof-of-concept for climate-aware digital-twin applications. Carrying forward from earlier this week: FAST-ML (September 22, Xiao et al.) for TC intensity, Bristol LPDM transfer learning for global GHG inversion (September 20), and the TAISE AI-driven catastrophe risk framework (September 15, US$130/50-year simulation).

items.headline: WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582) — Google DeepMind + Google Research: Operational Hourly Global Probabilistic Forecasts at 0.1° via Raw Geostationary Satellite Ingestion; Functional Generative Networks on Multiresolution Icosahedral Mesh; Powers Google Search + Google Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind + Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 [cs.LG] · Submitted 3 September 2026 · Operational
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 addresses two persistent shortcomings of earlier AI weather models: lower spatial/temporal resolution than physics-based NWP, and reliance on analysis (rather than raw observation) initialization. The model generates new probabilistic forecasts every hour by ingesting low-latency geostationary satellite imagery directly, achieving 0.1° spatial resolution for single-level variables (solar radiation, cloud cover) and 5 km for surface temperature and humidity — on par with operational physics-based global models. Architecture: Functional Generative Networks with an encode-process-decode structure operating on a multiresolution icosahedral mesh. WeatherNext 3 is now operationally deployed by Google, currently powering weather data in Google Search and Google Maps. The hourly update cycle and direct satellite ingestion eliminate the 6-hour analysis lag that constrains traditional AI model architectures.

items.headline: AICON (arXiv:2608.24651) — DWD’s Operational Global ML Weather Model at 13 km, 3-Hour Step; GNN Encoder-Processor-Decoder on Icosahedral Multi-Mesh; Trained on High-Resolution ICON-DREAM Dataset; Operational Since March 2, 2026; Fine-Scale Fidelity via No Multi-Step Rollout Training
items.meta: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) et al. · arXiv:2608.24651 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 25 August 2026 · Operational at DWD since 2 March 2026
items.summary: AICON is the German national meteorological service's operational global machine learning weather prediction model, generating forecasts at 13 km spatial resolution with a 3-hour time step. Architecture: a graph neural network with an encoder-processor-decoder structure using graph attention for node updates, operating on an icosahedral multi-mesh derived from ICON's native grid — ensuring consistency between training data representation and model inference. A key training design choice: AICON avoids autoregressive multi-step rollout and longer forecast horizons during training, prioritizing small-scale fidelity on the hypothesis that this preserves fine-scale features typically damped in models optimized for longer lead times. AICON entered full operational use at Deutscher Wetterdienst on March 2, 2026, making DWD one of the first national meteorological agencies to operationalize a purpose-built ML NWP model at high resolution.

items.headline: Sparse-Observation Atmospheric Thermal Forecasting With Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Climate-Aware Digital Twins (arXiv:2609.27290) — Chegini, Shivanian, Karimi, Dadgostari; RMSE Improvement 8.1% at 1-Hour to 23.8% at 3-Hour Lead vs. Baselines; Oklahoma ERA5 Case Study
items.meta: Chegini, Shivanian, Karimi, Dadgostari · arXiv:2609.27290 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 23 September 2026
items.summary: Reaches the design challenge for climate-aware digital twins: how to produce short-horizon (1–3 hour) atmospheric temperature forecasts at locations where conventional observations are sparse or absent. The authors evaluate a physics-informed neural network constrained by a pressure-coordinate thermodynamic advection–source equation; the diabatic-source closure is fit from the preceding 12-hour period and frozen before future-time training to prevent data leakage. Using hourly ERA5 reanalysis at three pressure levels evaluated as conditional hindcasts, the PINN achieves mean RMSE improvement over persistence and local-trend baselines growing from 8.1% at one hour to 23.8% at three hours in an Oklahoma development case. The result directly supports the climate-aware digital twin use case for built-environment operations, smart grids, and wildfire risk platforms requiring hyperlocal thermal forecasts in data-sparse regions.

items.headline: FAST-ML: Hybrid Physics–ML Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasting (arXiv:2609.25505) — Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi; Dual-Stream ERA5 Neural Parameterization Coupled to Differentiable FAST Intensity Model; End-to-End Optimization; Rapid Intensification Forecast
items.meta: Xiao, Lin, Ehrmann, Sarhadi · arXiv:2609.25505 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 22 September 2026
items.summary: FAST-ML bridges data-driven efficiency with physical constraints for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting, specifically targeting rapid intensification — one of the most consequential and poorly-forecast aspects of TC prediction. A physically-informed dual-stream neural parameterization ingests 3D ERA5 atmospheric fields to diagnose two key ventilation controls: environmental vertical wind shear and the mid-level entropy deficit. These parameters are fed into a differentiable implementation of the FAST intensity model, with parameters optimized end-to-end through the coupled architecture. By embedding physical constraints directly into the learning objective, FAST-ML ensures storm evolution remains governed by thermodynamic principles while benefiting from neural network flexibility. Directly relevant to the ongoing development of INVEST 91W.

items.headline: From Regional to Global: Transfer Learning for Atmospheric Transport Emulators (arXiv:2609.23838) — Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby (U Bristol); LPDM Emulator Extended from South America to Four Global Regions; ~1,000× Faster Than Physics-Based Model; Enables High-Resolution Satellite GHG Inversion at Scale
items.meta: Clark, Fillola, Keshtmand, Santos-Rodriguez, Rigby · arXiv:2609.23838 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 20 September 2026 · University of Bristol
items.summary: This paper evaluates whether a high-performance Lagrangian Particle Dispersion Model emulator previously developed for South America — running approximately 1,000× faster than the UK Met Office's NAME LPDM — can be spatially transferred to new regions via transfer learning. The authors evaluate spatial transferability across four world regions using both region-specific and multi-region models, establishing conditions under which transfer learning successfully extends the emulator without full retraining. The result opens a pathway toward global, high-resolution greenhouse gas inversion from modern satellite instruments (OCO-2, TROPOMI) at computational costs previously achievable only for regional domains.

items.headline: TAISE: AI-Driven Catastrophe Risk Modeling via Emergent Scenario Generation (arXiv:2609.16493) — Hang Gao; 50-Year Simulation on One GPU for US$130 with 2,000+ Cyclonic Events; Order-of-Magnitude Cost Reduction vs. Traditional CAT Models; Cross-Regional Correlations and Temporal Continuity Captured
items.summary: TAISE repurposes AI weather forecasting models (e.g. Pangu-Weather, GraphCast) to generate coherent continuous global atmospheric fields via self-iterative rollout, from which extreme events emerge rather than being manually constructed. A proof-of-concept 50-year simulation on a single GPU cost approximately US$130 and produced more than 2,000 cyclonic events — an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational cost versus conventional catastrophe modelling. The framework captures temporal continuity and cross-regional correlations absent in snapshot-based CAT model approaches. Directly applicable to the reinsurance/ILS sector, which has seen five consecutive years of insured nat-cat losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Heat-Related Labor Productivity Loss = US$41/tonne CO<sub>2</sub> (90% CI $1–108) — Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al.; Second-Largest SC-CO<sub>2</sub> Component After Heat Mortality; Agricultural Damage Revised Down to $29/tonne Using AR6
items.meta: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. · Nature Climate Change (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02749-z · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Moore, Haqiqi, Kong et al. quantify heat-related labor productivity loss as a standalone social cost of carbon component, finding a central estimate of US$41 per tonne CO₂ (90% CI $1–108) — the second-largest SC-CO₂ component after heat mortality. Agricultural damage was simultaneously revised down from US$95 to US$29 per tonne CO₂ using IPCC AR6 methods and updated dose-response functions. Losses are geographically concentrated in South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. Immediate implications for climate damage assessments used in litigation and regulatory cost-benefit analysis.

items.source: Geophysical Research Letters / AGU / PIK Potsdam
items.headline: GRL Vol. 53 Issue 17: “Global Warming Has Accelerated Significantly” — Foster & Rahmstorf; >98% Confidence; Fastest Decade of Any in 177-Year Record Across Five Datasets After ENSO/Volcanic/Solar Removal
items.meta: Foster & Rahmstorf · Geophysical Research Letters (2026) · Vol. 53, Issue 17 · doi:10.1029/2025GL118804 · Published 16 September 2026
items.summary: Foster and Rahmstorf apply natural-variability filtering across five global temperature datasets to isolate the forced warming signal from ENSO, volcanic, and solar variability. The residual shows, for the first time with greater than 98% statistical confidence, that global warming has accelerated since approximately 2015 at a rate faster than any previous decade in the 177-year record. The implied non-linearity is consistent with compound forcing from cumulative CO₂, declining reflective aerosol loading as Asian coal combustion falls, and positive ice-albedo and water vapor feedbacks.

items.headline: Nature Communications: Hunga Tonga Stratospheric Aerosol Layer Catalysed CH<sub>4</sub> Oxidation at 900±220 Mg/day Via Cl-Radical Pathway — 12 ppb HCHO at 30 km; Pathway Absent From All CMIP7 Models; Implications for SAI and Large-Eruption Scenarios
items.meta: van Herpen et al. · Nature Communications (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72191-4 · Published 15 September 2026
items.summary: Van Herpen et al. show that the 2022 Hunga Tonga eruption's stratospheric sulphate aerosol layer catalysed a previously uncharacterised methane oxidation pathway involving Cl radicals produced at aerosol surfaces. Using ACE-FTS and MIPAS observations, the authors quantify CH₄ oxidation at 900 ± 220 Mg/day between 25–35 km, sufficient to explain the anomalous HCHO column of ~12 ppb at 30 km (~8× background). The mechanism is absent from current CMIP7 chemistry–climate models; if triggered by large eruptions or proposed stratospheric aerosol injection, it could constitute a net cooling offset not captured in climate sensitivity assessments or geoengineering scenario modelling.

items.title: Kairos Power Secures Up to $100 Million from Samsung C&T for Google Hermes 2 Nuclear Reactor Build — $70 M Equity + $30 M In-Kind Engineering; 50 MW Fluoride Salt-Cooled Demonstration Plant at Oak Ridge; Operations Target 2030
items.body_html: Kairos Power and Samsung C&T agreed on September 21 to a binding term sheet under which Samsung C&T will provide up to $100 million — $70 million in direct equity plus $30 million in in-kind engineering and procurement services — to support the delivery of Kairos’s 50 MW fluoride salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (KP-FHR) Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Hermes 2 is purpose-built to supply firm low-carbon baseload power for Google’s AI data centres under a previously announced clean-power purchase agreement; Samsung C&T has built or helped build approximately a dozen nuclear reactors globally and brings direct reactor construction execution capability that Kairos has not previously had in-house. The investment is subject to regulatory approvals and scheduled for completion in 2030. The deal is the latest example of data-centre developers driving demand for firm low-carbon baseload sources — a pattern CTVC identified as the dominant force behind the 55% surge in H1 2026 climate-tech VC.
items.source_html: TechCrunch / World Nuclear News

items.title: Rainmaker Raises $100 Million Series B for Drone-Based Cloud Seeding — Led by NOA VC + Upfront; DCVC, Lowercarbon, Dream Ventures Co-Invest; Pitches Cloud Seeding as Adaptation Tech for Data Center Water Demand and Drought Relief
items.body_html: Rainmaker, the El Segundo, California weather-modification startup, announced a $100 million Series B on September 21 led by NOA VC and Upfront Ventures with co-investment from DCVC, Lowercarbon Capital, and Dream Ventures — bringing total funding to $150.3 million since its 2023 founding. Rainmaker deploys custom drone fleets to seed clouds with silver iodide or other nucleating agents; the company frames cloud seeding as climate adaptation rather than geoengineering, targeting drought relief in the American West and cooling and humidification services for water-hungry hyperscale data centers. The round will fund atmospheric research team expansion, drone fleet development, and commercial trials in the Southwest.
items.source_html: Fast Company / PR Newswire

items.title: CTVC / Currence H1’26 Climate Tech Report: $26.1 Billion Global VC in H1 2026 (+55% YoY); Data Centers 34% of Total; Deal Count at 5-Year Low (-25%); Series A up 55% to $4.5 Bn; Adaptation Funding +64% — Fastest-Growing Sub-Vertical
items.body_html: CTVC (now Currence) published its H1’26 Climate Tech Investment & Innovation Report on September 21, 2026, finding total global venture investment reached $26.1 billion in H1 2026 — up 55% year-on-year and the strongest first half since 2022 — driven overwhelmingly by data-centre infrastructure. The Built Environment category grew more than 800% and overtook Energy as the largest funding vertical, with the “speed-to-power race” driving data-centre developers toward low-carbon firm power sources — advanced nuclear, superhot geothermal, long-duration storage — as gas turbine lead times stretch to 5–8 years. Deal count fell 25% to a 5-year low; the 10 largest rounds took 42% of all H1 2026 investment. Series A rose 55% to $4.5 billion on nuclear appetite; adaptation funding grew 64% — the fastest-growing sub-vertical — consistent with the accelerating Super El Niño and record-insured-loss environment.

items.title: Cat Bond and ILS Market Bulletin (Week Ending September 20): MembersCap Launches First Cat Bond Fund + Novel ILW; Gallagher Securities Developing First-Ever New-Peril Cat Bond; CalPERS ILS Holdings Approach US$2.5 Billion — Fifth Consecutive Year of >$100 Billion Global Insured Nat-Cat Losses
items.body_html: The Artemis weekly bulletin for the week ending September 20, 2026 highlights three developments in the catastrophe bond and ILS market: MembersCap launched the first dedicated cat bond fund strategy alongside a novel industry loss warranty (ILW) structure designed to expand ILS investor access; Gallagher Securities is developing the first-ever cat bond covering a previously unbondable peril, representing a structural expansion of the cat bond market’s risk frontier; and CalPERS’ insurance-linked securities holdings are approaching US$2.5 billion at mid-year 2026, cementing its position as the largest institutional investor in the cat bond asset class — all in the context of the fifth consecutive year of global insured natural catastrophe losses exceeding US$100 billion.

items.title: Mazama Energy Raises $135 Million Series B for Superhot Engineered Geothermal — Led by Centaurus Capital + Doerr Capital; ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla, Gates Frontier Co-Invest; Project Athena Targeting 750°F (400°C) at Newberry Volcano, Oregon
items.body_html: Mazama Energy raised $135 million in an oversubscribed Series B announced September 17, co-led by Centaurus Capital (John Arnold’s fund) and Doerr Capital. ConocoPhillips, Shell Ventures, Khosla Ventures, Gates Frontier, SiteGround Capital, H. Barton Asset Management, and the Jeffrey and Marieke Rothschild Foundation also participated. Mazama holds the record for the hottest EGS ever built — a 629°F (331°C) well at Newberry Volcano in 2025; Project Athena targets 750°F (400°C), where a single well can deliver up to 10× the power of a conventional 390°F well using 75% less water and 80% fewer wells — attributes increasingly attractive to data-center developers seeking firm low-carbon baseload.

items.title: EU Climate Insurance Alliance — Von der Leyen State of the Union September 16: Only 25% of European Catastrophe Losses Currently Insured; Parametric + Group Instruments Proposed; 100 Vulnerable EU Regions Mapped by October; Alliance Faces Criticism for Lacking Mandatory Cover Mandate
items.body_html: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the European Climate Insurance Alliance in her September 16 State of the Union address, citing data showing only 25% of European catastrophic climate losses are currently insured. The Alliance will develop group insurance pools for currently uninsurable catastrophe risks and expand parametric instruments for agriculture, coastal flooding, and wildfire; the European Commission will map the 100 most-vulnerable EU regions by October 2026. The announcement follows Europe’s wildfire season reaching 668,035 ha per EFFIS, with uninsured losses estimated at €40–60 billion. Critics noted the Alliance would not close the protection gap without mandatory natural-hazard cover.
items.source_html: Green Central Banking / The Insurer

items.title: Laki Power Raises €6 Million Series A Led by NATO Innovation Fund — Iceland Grid Monitoring Device Self-Powered From Live HV Lines; NIF’s First Iceland Investment; + ReykVC
items.body_html: Laki Power, a Reykjavík-based grid monitoring hardware company, closed a €6 million Series A on September 16 led by the NATO Innovation Fund with co-investment from ReykVC — NIF’s first investment in an Icelandic company. Laki Power’s core product harvests its operating power directly from live high-voltage transmission lines via inductive energy harvesting, eliminating external power supplies and batteries; the device provides real-time line-current, temperature, sag, and fault-location data — directly relevant to Nordic and Arctic grid resilience and NATO dual-use energy security.
